what_its_for: Spinosad is a medicated lotion used to treat head lice (tiny insects that live in hair and on the scalp). It kills lice and their eggs to help get rid of the infestation.
how_to_take: Apply the lotion directly to dry hair and scalp. Start at the scalp and work the lotion through the hair all the way to the ends. Leave it on for exactly 10 minutes, then rinse it off thoroughly with warm water. You do NOT need to use a nit comb after treatment. Wash your hands well after applying. Avoid getting the lotion in your eyes, nose, or mouth. If contact with eyes occurs, rinse with water right away.
dosing: Apply one treatment to dry hair and scalp and leave on for 10 minutes before rinsing. If live lice are still seen 7 days after the first treatment, a second treatment may be applied. Do not use more than two treatments unless your doctor tells you to. The amount used depends on hair length: use just enough to fully coat the hair and scalp. Typical amounts range from about half a bottle to a full bottle for longer or thicker hair.
missed_dose: Spinosad is used as a single treatment, not on a daily schedule. If you forget to do your second treatment on the recommended day (day 7 after the first treatment), apply it as soon as you remember. Do not use it more often than directed by your doctor.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and open flames, as this product is flammable. Keep the bottle tightly closed and out of reach of children. Do not freeze. Throw away any unused lotion safely — do not pour it down the drain or throw it in household trash without checking local disposal guidelines.
what_to_avoid: Do not use near open flames or while smoking, as this lotion is flammable until it is fully dry. Avoid getting the lotion in your eyes, nose, or mouth. Do not share personal items such as hats, combs, brushes, or pillowcases, as this can spread lice to others. Wash all recently used clothing, bedding, towels, and hats in hot water and dry on high heat to help prevent re-infestation. Avoid using other hair products (such as conditioner) on the day of treatment, as they may reduce how well the lotion works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if: live lice are still present more than 7 days after your second treatment; you notice signs of a skin or scalp reaction such as redness, swelling, itching, or rash that is getting worse; your child develops eye irritation that does not go away after rinsing with water; or if you have any questions about whether the treatment worked.
when_it_works: Spinosad starts killing lice quickly after it is applied. Many people see results after just one treatment. If live lice are still seen after 7 days, a second treatment can be used. You may still see dead lice or nit shells (egg casings) in the hair after treatment — this is normal and does not mean the treatment failed.
special_populations: Children: Spinosad lotion is approved for use in children 6 months of age and older. Always have an adult apply the product to children. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this product if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. While it is applied to the skin and not taken by mouth, your doctor can help you decide if it is safe for you. Elderly: No special dosing changes are needed for older adults, but ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any concerns.
